facts.text: It was named East Melbourne in 1837 by Port Phillip District surveyor Robert Hoddle, but was not actually settled until 1840.
Historically, East Melbourne was the original home to Scotch College, St Patrick's College, and Parade College.
East Melbourne has two main rail stations: Parliament underground on Spring Street and Jolimont on the Hurstbridge and Mernda lines, serving MCG crowds.
Attention was focused on East Melbourne's built heritage and nearly all of East Melbourne was specified as an historic precinct in the Register of the National Estate, 1981.
Among the first settlers was Charles La Trobe, who built a transportable dwelling in 1840 and wealthy professionals followed, establishing mansions there.
